$comment: Machine-readable surface contract for all w6w wrappers. Source of truth for conformance tests. Keep in sync with docs/endpoints.md.
$basePathComment: Empty since 0.2.0: the server serves its routes at the ROOT of its own host (https://api.w6w.io/vars, not .../api/vars). Clients append nothing to the configured origin.

operations.name: me
operations.summary: Caller identity plus w6w component versions.
operations.notes: Fixed 2026-07-28: the wrapper calls `/auth/me` directly — the server’s real, already-live identity route (verified live: 200, `{tenant, subject, account, role}`), not the not-yet-built `/api/me` alias D15 originally specced. `{tenant, subject, account, role}`. The response body is flat, NOT a `{user:{…}}` envelope. The live consumer is the reference studio; a nested envelope would break it. `versions` is optional and additive. The server now sends two keys inside it: `server` (the deployment’s image version, equal to `GET /version`’s `version`) and `composition` (equal to `GET /version`’s `composition`, a per-repo short-SHA string, `"dev"` for local builds). A wrapper must still tolerate `versions` being absent entirely (an older server) and must tolerate unknown keys inside it. `versions.wrapper` is filled client-side from the wrapper’s own package version. PRECEDENCE IS SERVER-WINS: the wrapper’s own version is only a DEFAULT that any key the server supplied overrides — `{ wrapper: VERSION, ...body.versions }` in TS, `{"wrapper": VERSION, **(body.get("versions") or {})}` in Python. Do NOT write the other order (`{**server, wrapper: VERSION}`), which would make the wrapper’s value win; the two are observably different on the one field a bug report is read off. DISPLAY IS A SEPARATE RULE: a wrapper must never SHOW a version of `0.0.0` or empty — if the resolved value is `0.0.0` or empty string, it presents `"dev"` (D5). The two rules do not conflict, because they act at different layers: server-wins governs the VALUE carried in the returned object (which stays a faithful transcription of the wire), the display rule governs what a banner such as `w6w info` PRINTS. So a server sending `versions.wrapper: "0.0.0"` is carried through in the data and rendered as `dev` to the user. D8 — the operation name is `me`; `w6w info` is a CLI alias only (see `cliAlias`). At 0.18.0 the body may carry `capabilities: { userScopedCredentials?: boolean }`; gate on `=== true` (absent = an older server).

operations.name: connections.list
operations.summary: List the caller's connections (credentials redacted).
operations.notes: `credential` is redacted server-side and must not appear in the wrapper's list type. D4 — kept in v0.1.0 even though the 07-27 intake does not name it: without it a user has no way to discover a `conn_…` URN to pass to `run`. Verified live. Each row carries `tenant` + `subject` (not `owner`) and a top-level `app` object (`displayName` plus optional `iconSvg`, `iconSvgDark`, `brandColor`, `brandColorDark`) beside `appId`; `app` is `null` when the server found no app row, and absent from an older server. `builtIn` is an optional boolean: `true` marks the synthetic zero-credential row (a `zerocred:` id, usable with no connection step, not stored and not deletable); it is absent on stored connections and on an older server that does not emit it. `credentialId` (added in contract 0.13.0) is `string | null`, always present on a server that has the credential resource: the id of the stored credential this connection uses, and `null` = no stored credential (tenantAuth, jit, none, or a zero-credential row). Credential management itself stays console-only (`client.console.credentials.*`), not an operation here. At 0.18.0 each row may carry `accessScope: "account" | "user"` (absent = an older server; `subject` stays creator attribution). The server-side `?accessScope=` filter exists but is not a param of this op in 0.18.0. At 0.19.0 each row may carry the connection's keep-alive state, none of it secret: `autoRefresh: boolean` (background credential refresh on or off; the server defaults it to true), `lastRefreshedAt: string | null` (ISO; the last successful refresh or the original grant; `null` when unknown) and `refreshFailingSince: string | null` (ISO; the first failure of the current streak of failing background refreshes; `null` when not failing). `lastRefreshedAt` is no longer redacted (contracts before 0.19.0 said it was). All three are absent from an older server and from the synthetic `builtIn` row, so wrappers type them optional (TS `?:`, Python `None`). `state: "broken"` is now also set at once when a refresh is refused in a way that needs a new sign-in, and after background refreshes have failed for 3 days.

operations.name: connections.get
operations.summary: Fetch one connection (credentials redacted).
operations.notes: Server wraps the body as `{ connection: ConnectionSummary }`; the wrapper unwraps it. Same projection as `connections.list` (the credential redacted, the keep-alive fields present). Account-owned: another account's id is the uniform `404 unknown_connection`, indistinguishable from an id that does not exist. The built-in zero-credential row that `connections.list` can include (a `zerocred:` id, `builtIn: true`) is synthetic and is not fetchable: `404`. `credentialId` (added in contract 0.13.0) is `string | null`, always present on a server that has the credential resource: the id of the stored credential this connection uses, and `null` = no stored credential (tenantAuth, jit, none, or a zero-credential row). Credential management itself stays console-only (`client.console.credentials.*`), not an operation here. At 0.18.0 the row may carry `accessScope: "account" | "user"` (absent = an older server; `subject` stays creator attribution). The server-side `?accessScope=` filter exists but is not a param of this op in 0.18.0. At 0.19.0 each row may carry the connection's keep-alive state, none of it secret: `autoRefresh: boolean` (background credential refresh on or off; the server defaults it to true), `lastRefreshedAt: string | null` (ISO; the last successful refresh or the original grant; `null` when unknown) and `refreshFailingSince: string | null` (ISO; the first failure of the current streak of failing background refreshes; `null` when not failing). `lastRefreshedAt` is no longer redacted (contracts before 0.19.0 said it was). All three are absent from an older server and from the synthetic `builtIn` row, so wrappers type them optional (TS `?:`, Python `None`). `state: "broken"` is now also set at once when a refresh is refused in a way that needs a new sign-in, and after background refreshes have failed for 3 days.

operations.name: connections.delete
operations.summary: Delete a connection.
operations.notes: The server returns `{ok: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code), same pin as `documents.delete`. Keeps the server's authorization: the connection must be owned by the caller's account; another account's id is the uniform `404 unknown_connection` and destroys nothing, and so is a `zerocred:` built-in row (it is not stored). Not idempotent: a second delete is `404`. Before the row is removed the server tears down every trigger subscription bound to the connection (the vendor webhook is removed while the credential can still sign the call). While live callables (Functions/Endpoints) still use the connection the server refuses with `409 connection_in_use`, body `{ error: { code, message, dependents } }` where `dependents = { callables: [{ id, kind, key, displayName, enabled, sites }], subscriptions: [{ id, appId, triggerKey, workflowId }], routes: [{ id, name, project, status }] }` (`routes` are model routes bound to the connection; a routes-only dependent also refuses); it surfaces as the lane's ordinary API error and the caller reads `dependents` from its parsed body. `force` is sent as `?force=true` ONLY when true (false/omitted sends no query string): a forced delete disables the dependent callables (never edits them) and still succeeds; it also marks dependent model routes `broken`, and the success body then carries `{ ok: true, disabled: [...], brokenRoutes: string[] }` and the wrapper still unwraps to nothing. Subscriptions are torn down either way and never cause the 409. Creating, updating, testing and OAuth-connecting a connection are NOT in this contract.

operations.name: workflows.list
operations.summary: List the caller's workflow definitions.
operations.notes: `tag` (query, optional) narrows the list to callables carrying that tag: a row is kept when one of its tags equals the value or starts with the value plus `.` (segment-bounded: `action.order` matches `action.order` and `action.order.confirm` but not `action.orders`). Sent as `?tag=<value>` ONLY when set and non-empty (an omitted or empty tag sends no query parameter, which is the unfiltered list); a single value, no multi-tag OR. Unpaginated today. Return a container type that can grow a cursor without a breaking change. D4 — kept in v0.1.0: it is how a user discovers a `wf_…` URN to pass to `run`. Verified live.

operations.name: workflows.run
operations.summary: Enqueue a workflow run; optionally wait for a terminal state.

params.name: trigger
params.$comment: `knownValues` is DOCUMENTATION, not a constraint. `closedEnum: false` — wrappers type this as a plain string and must NOT validate against the list; the server may add a sixth value and a wrapper that hard-codes the enum would reject a request the server accepts.

naming.python: client.workflows.run(id, wait=False, variables=None, trigger=None, input=None, allow_unpublished=False, entry=None)

operations.notes: 202 is a normal outcome, not an error: the run is still queued/running. A failed run returns 200 with status 'failed' and must NOT raise. `trigger` is a STRING, not an object: the server reads it as a `RunTrigger` (`"manual" | "schedule" | "webhook" | "event" | "replay"` today), and it defaults to 'manual' server-side when omitted. The five values are recorded in `knownValues` as documentation only — every wrapper types the param as an open string (`trigger?: string` / `trigger: str | None`) and passes it through unvalidated, so a sixth server value needs no wrapper release. `variables` and `input` are NOT interchangeable: `variables` seeds the run's variable scope, read downstream as `vars.*`; `input` is delivered to the entry trigger node's own recorded output, read downstream as `nodes.<triggerId>.output.<key>` — the shape a trigger's declared fields actually arrive in (`steps.<triggerId>.output.<key>` is the permanent alias for the same value, so either name reads it). D4 — kept alongside the unified `run`, which is deliberately narrower: `?wait=`, `variables`, `trigger` and `input` have no slot in the three-field `{urn, action, payload}` shape. Verified live. `allowUnpublished` (body, optional boolean) runs the STORED definition even if it was never published — the draft run (a disabled one is still refused). It is sent only when `true` (never `false`) and runs the stored row exactly as last saved, never a body the caller submits, so a caller must save first. Without it the run needs a published workflow (409 `workflow_not_published`); a disabled workflow is refused either way (409 `workflow_disabled`). Without allowUnpublished the call still executes the STORED row as last saved: a published version is a precondition, not what runs; use runVersion to execute a published snapshot. The run response carries its per-node records under `nodes` (keyed by node id, canonical) and again under `steps` (the alias, the same values) — read either, they never disagree; a `202` carries neither map, and a wrapper normalises `nodes` to `{}`. A failed node's error record carries `nodeId`, with `stepId` beside it holding the same id.

operations.name: workflows.cancel
operations.summary: Cancel a queued or running workflow run.
operations.notes: Addressed by the RUN id, not the workflow id — the path root is `/runs/…`, a deliberate exception to this class's otherwise `/workflows/…`-rooted paths, because a workflow can have many runs and only the run id picks one out. `202` means the cancellation was REQUESTED, not that the run has stopped: the server does not wait for the transition, so the returned `status` is the run's status AS IT IS NOW — still `queued` or `running` — and a wrapper must never report it as `"canceled"`. Idempotent: repeating the cancel on a run that is already marked but not yet terminal is still `202`. `404 unknown_run` covers both "no such run" and "not your workflow", indistinguishable on purpose. `409 run_not_cancelable` when the run has already reached a terminal state.

operations.name: workflows.get
operations.summary: Fetch one workflow's stored definition.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `wf_…` id. The response body IS the payload — `{workflow, sourceRef, updatedAt}`, with no envelope key to peel, so `unwrap` does not apply here. `workflow` is the stored definition overlaid with the authoritative `status` and `tags` columns, and it stays OPAQUE in every lane (`Record<string, unknown>` / `dict`): its `nodes[]` carry node types the engine owns and extends, and a wrapper that modelled them would reject a workflow a newer server accepts. Definitions are stored and returned as `nodes[]`; a write may send `steps[]` instead, carrying the same per-node records, but a body with both arrays — or with neither — is refused `400 invalid_workflow`. **`updatedAt` is a TOP-LEVEL SIBLING of `workflow`, never a field inside it** — the definition is the portable document and a server timestamp must not enter it; it is also the optimistic-concurrency token that `workflows.update` takes as `ifUnmodifiedSince`. Missing id is `404 unknown_workflow`.

operations.name: workflows.create
operations.summary: Create a workflow definition.
operations.notes: Addressed by nothing — this is the create half of the server's single upsert route (`POST /workflows`), which is why `create` and `update` share a method and a path here. THE SERVER MINTS AN ID ONLY WHEN THE CALLER SENDS NONE: `validateDefinition` accepts a body with no `id` (the server mints `wf_<uuid>` itself) and accepts a caller-supplied `id` only if it matches `^wf_[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}$`, else `400 invalid_workflow`. Every wrapper still mints one client-side (`wf_<uuid>`) when the definition carries none, and forwards an `id` the caller supplied untouched, so what it sends already satisfies that grammar. `definition` is sent VERBATIM as the body, never wrapped in an envelope key. `manifestVersion` must be `"2"`. A definition whose `trigger.cron` is set also (re)applies a schedule, reported back as `scheduled`.

operations.name: workflows.update
operations.summary: Overwrite a workflow definition.
operations.notes: The update half of the same upsert route as `workflows.create`. **A FULL REPLACEMENT, NOT A PATCH** — the server stores what it is given, so a field left out is a field removed; read with `workflows.get`, change what you mean to change, send the whole thing back. `id` comes from the FIRST ARGUMENT and is pinned into the body, overriding any `id` the definition carries: trusting the body makes `update("wf_a", defOfB)` silently write to B. `ifUnmodifiedSince` is the optimistic-concurrency precondition, sent as the `x-w6w-if-unmodified-since` HEADER (not a query param) and ONLY when a value was given — never as an empty or "null" string, which the server answers `400 invalid_precondition`. Pass the exact `updatedAt` from `workflows.get` or a prior save; a stale one is `409 workflow_stale`, which IS recoverable by reloading and re-saving, unlike `409 workflow_conflict`, which is not.

operations.name: workflows.archive
operations.summary: Archive a workflow — the required step before deleting it.
operations.notes: One-way: there is no unarchive route on this domain. Idempotent — archiving an already-archived workflow re-returns it unchanged rather than erroring, so a wrapper must not special-case the second call. Returns the definition under a `workflow` envelope, in the same merged shape `workflows.get` returns. This is a PRECONDITION of `workflows.delete`, not a convenience: the delete refuses anything still `draft` or `active`. Missing id is `404 unknown_workflow`.

operations.name: workflows.delete
operations.summary: Delete an archived workflow.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `wf_…` id. The server returns `{ok: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING — declared return is `void` (`Promise<void>` in TS, `None` in Python, no stdout payload in the CLI beyond an exit code), the same pin `documents.delete` carries; `Ok` is not a public wrapper type. The workflow's runs, schedules and subscriptions cascade-delete server-side. **ARCHIVE FIRST**: a workflow that is not `archived` yet is `409 workflow_not_archived`, and a wrapper must NOT catch that and archive on the caller's behalf — a two-step destructive path completed silently is how a caller deletes something they only meant to look at. Deleting an unknown id is `404 unknown_workflow`, not a silent success.

operations.name: workflows.listVersions
operations.summary: List a workflow's published versions.
operations.notes: Returns the WHOLE body unchanged: `enabled`, `currentPublishedVersion` (`null` before the first publish) and `versions[]` (`versionNumber`, `createdAt`, `createdBy` — `null` when unknown — and `isCurrentPublished`). Metadata only: no `definition`; fetch one with `workflows.getVersion`. Missing id is `404 unknown_workflow`.

operations.name: workflows.getVersion
operations.summary: Read one published version of a workflow, with its definition.
operations.notes: The server answers `{version: {versionNumber, createdAt, createdBy, isCurrentPublished, definition}}` and the wrapper UNWRAPS the `version` key. `definition` is opaque and redacted server-side (a sealed secret envelope is never returned). `n` is the 1-based version number. Errors: `404 unknown_version`, `404 unknown_workflow`, `400 invalid_version` when `n` is not a positive integer.

operations.name: workflows.publish
operations.summary: Publish the workflow's stored definition as a new immutable version.
operations.notes: Returns the WHOLE body: `{version: {kind, callableId, versionNumber, createdAt, createdBy}, currentPublishedVersion}`. Publish snapshots the STORED row, not whatever an editor holds in memory, so a caller must flush any pending save first. Publishing a workflow also makes it active (it flips a never-published workflow to `active`). No precondition is taken: nothing checks that the row changed since the last publish. Errors: `404 unknown_workflow`.

operations.name: workflows.revert
operations.summary: Rewrite the live workflow from a published version.
operations.notes: The server answers `{reverted: {kind, callableId, versionNumber}}` and the wrapper UNWRAPS the `reverted` key. Revert REWRITES the live row from the chosen version, so its `updatedAt` moves: a following `workflows.update` that passes `ifUnmodifiedSince` needs the freshly read `updatedAt` (`workflows.get`), not the one from before the revert, or it is `409 workflow_stale`. It does not publish: the live row becomes a draft that matches version `n` until `workflows.publish` is called. Errors: `404 unknown_version`, `404 unknown_workflow`, `400 invalid_version`.

operations.name: workflows.enable
operations.summary: Enable the workflow's invocability.
operations.notes: The server returns `{enabled: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code). Idempotent. A disabled workflow is refused by every run, version runs and `allowUnpublished` draft runs included (`workflow_disabled`). Missing id is `404 unknown_workflow`.

operations.name: workflows.disable
operations.summary: Disable the workflow's invocability.
operations.notes: The server returns `{enabled: false}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code). Idempotent. A disabled workflow is refused by every run, version runs and `allowUnpublished` draft runs included (`workflow_disabled`). Missing id is `404 unknown_workflow`.

operations.name: workflows.runVersion
operations.summary: Run one published version of a workflow.

naming.python: client.workflows.run_version(id, n, wait=False, variables=None, trigger=None, input=None)

operations.notes: Same body and `?wait=` as `workflows.run`, against ONE published version instead of the live row: the run executes that version's definition. Returns the same `RunResult` shape `workflows.run` does (200 terminal, 202 queued/running; a failed run is 200 with status 'failed' and must NOT raise). `wait` is sent as `?wait=true` only when `true`. There is no `allowUnpublished` here — a version is published by definition. Errors: `404 unknown_version`, `404 unknown_workflow`, `409 workflow_archived`, `409 workflow_disabled`, `409 workflow_not_published`, `400 invalid_version`.

operations.name: documents.list
operations.summary: List the caller's documents in a project.
operations.notes: Server wraps the body as `{ documents: Doc[] }`; the wrapper unwraps and returns the array. Documents ARE project-scoped: every `documents.*` route accepts an optional `?project=` and otherwise resolves the account's default project. An unknown project id is `400 unknown_project`.

operations.name: documents.get
operations.summary: Fetch one document by its `doc_…` id.
operations.notes: Addressed by the server-issued `doc_…` id, not by `key` (D6 — wrappers mirror the server's addressing exactly). Server wraps the body as `{ document: Doc }`; the wrapper unwraps. Missing id is `404 unknown_document`.

operations.name: documents.getByKey
operations.summary: Fetch one document by its human-chosen `key`.
operations.notes: `DocumentsRepo.getByKey` already existed and was already called by `POST /documents` for its conflict check; only the HTTP route was missing. D12 (amending D6) — a user who chose a key should be able to address by it, and the alternative leaks internal `doc_…` ids to users who never saw them. NO client-side list-then-filter: `packages/wrappers/README.md` "What a wrapper is" forbids composing two calls to make an operation useful. Same wrap/unwrap and `404 unknown_document` as `documents.get`. Server-implemented 2026-07-28: the route trims the incoming key to match what `POST /documents` stores, and creation rejects a key of exactly "." or ".." — the one class no HTTP client can round-trip through a URL path segment (percent-encoding is a no-op on `.`, and different clients disagree on dot-segment collapse).

operations.name: documents.create
operations.summary: Create a document under a caller-chosen `key`.
operations.notes: Create is addressed by `key` (D6 — mirror the server: create by key, update/delete by id). `key` is a non-empty string of at most 128 characters, unique per scope+project. `content` is raw text and is never parsed. `format` is one of text|markdown|yaml|html|json and defaults to 'text'; it is a hint only and does not gate the content. Duplicate key is `409 document_exists` — wrappers must surface that code, not swallow it into a generic error.

operations.name: documents.update
operations.summary: Patch a document's content, format or description.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `doc_…` id, NOT by `key` (D6). `key` itself is immutable — it is not in the patch body. Every field is optional; an omitted field is left alone. Missing id is `404 unknown_document`.

operations.name: documents.delete
operations.summary: Delete a document.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `doc_…` id (D6). The server returns `{ ok: true }`, but the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING: the declared return is `void` (`Promise<void>` in TS, `None` in Python, no stdout payload in the CLI beyond an exit code). `Ok` is not a public wrapper type — see docs/implementation.md §5. Deleting an unknown id is `404 unknown_document`, not a silent success — the delete is not idempotent and wrappers must not pretend otherwise.

operations.name: vars.list
operations.summary: List the caller's typed variables.
operations.notes: Vars are NOT project-scoped — unlike documents, no `vars.*` route accepts `?project=` (verified: no `vars` route reads it). They are scoped by tenant/subject only. Do not add a `project` option to any `vars.*` signature; adding one later would be additive, faking one now would be a lie the server does not honour. Server wraps the body as `{ vars: Var[] }`; the wrapper unwraps.

operations.name: vars.get
operations.summary: Fetch one variable by its `var_…` id.
operations.notes: Addressed by the server-issued `var_…` id, not by `name` (D6). Server wraps the body as `{ var: Var }`; the wrapper unwraps — note the singular key is `var`, which is a reserved word in TypeScript and must be read as a property, never destructured into a binding of that name. Missing id is `404 unknown_var`.

operations.name: vars.getByName
operations.summary: Fetch one variable by its human-chosen `name`.
operations.notes: `VarsRepo.getByName` already existed and was already called by `POST /vars` for its conflict check; only the HTTP route was missing. D12 (amending D6) — key-addressed reads become server routes rather than client-side composition; `packages/wrappers/README.md` "What a wrapper is" forbids a list-then-filter workaround. Same `404 unknown_var` as `vars.get`. Server-implemented 2026-07-28: names are already regex-validated (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, case-sensitive) at create time, which is URL-safe by construction — no extra hazard handling needed.

operations.name: vars.create
operations.summary: Create a typed variable under a caller-chosen `name`.
operations.notes: Create is addressed by `name` (D6 — mirror the server: create by name, update/delete by id). `name` must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` (case-sensitive: `HELP_EMAIL` and `help_email` are different names); violations are `400 invalid_name`. `type` is one of string|number|boolean|json and `value` is validated against it server-side (`400 invalid_type` / `400 invalid_value`). Duplicate name is `409 var_exists` — wrappers must surface that code, not swallow it into a generic error. No `project` param: vars are not project-scoped.

operations.name: vars.update
operations.summary: Patch a variable's type, value or description.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `var_…` id, NOT by `name` (D6). `name` itself is immutable — it is not in the patch body. A `value` sent without a `type` is validated against the variable's EXISTING type. Missing id is `404 unknown_var`. No `project` param: vars are not project-scoped.

operations.name: vars.delete
operations.summary: Delete a variable.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `var_…` id (D6). The server returns `{ ok: true }`, but the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING: the declared return is `void` (`Promise<void>` in TS, `None` in Python, no stdout payload in the CLI beyond an exit code). `Ok` is not a public wrapper type — see docs/implementation.md §5. Deleting an unknown id is `404 unknown_var`, not a silent success. No `project` param: vars are not project-scoped.

operations.name: functions.run
operations.summary: Run one Function by its key (or id) and return its output.
operations.notes: The NAME IS THE FIRST ARGUMENT in every lane, matching `workflows.run(id, opts?)`, so all three runnable kinds read alike; it is not a field inside an options object. Wrappers expose the body field as `payload` even though the wire spells it `inputs` — one word across every runnable kind, and reconciling that inconsistency is precisely the wrapper's job (the Endpoint operation below spells the same concept `input`). Returns the Function's OUTPUT, not a kind-discriminated envelope: the kind is settled by the operation name, so a discriminant would be a field the caller unwraps to learn nothing. A `null` output is a SUCCESSFUL run, not a malformed body — a Function's output is an opaque pass-through and an action that returns nothing yields `{"output": null}` — so a wrapper must guard on PRESENCE of the `output` key rather than on its truthiness. 422 `function_incomplete` when the Function has no runnable `impl`. The `{idOrKey}` path segment takes EITHER the resource's host-issued id or the key the user gave it, with no prefix, flag or tag to say which — the two shapes cannot collide, because an id carries a kind prefix and therefore an underscore while a key is a kebab-slug that forbids one. Resolution is id-first (a pure prefix test, no query), so this path cannot be used to probe whether a key exists by supplying something id-shaped. Two unknown KEYS answer identically and neither is echoed back — a key is short, human-chosen and guessable, so echoing it would make this an enumeration oracle; an unknown id may still be echoed, since nobody guesses a uuid. The key is unique per ACCOUNT, so within the scope a credential carries it names exactly one resource. INVOCATION FRAME (server, 2026-08-20): the 200 body is now `{kind:"function", output, invocationId, status, startedAt, finishedAt, durationMs}`. `output` keeps its name, its position and its opaque-pass-through meaning, so the "guard on PRESENCE of `output`" rule above is unchanged and a wrapper that unwraps `output` needs no change at all. The added fields are the attempt's own record: `invocationId` resolves through `GET /invocations/{id}` to the stored inputs, output and timing, and a FAILED call's 4xx body carries the same fields beside its `error`. `allowUnpublished` (body, optional boolean) invokes the STORED definition even if it was never published — the draft run (a disabled one is still refused). It is sent only when `true` (never `false`) and runs the row exactly as last saved, never a body the caller submits, so a caller must save first. Without it the call needs a published Function (422 `function_not_published`); a disabled Function is refused either way (422 `function_disabled`). Without allowUnpublished the call still executes the STORED row as last saved: a published version is a precondition, not what runs; use runVersion to execute a published snapshot.

operations.name: functions.list
operations.summary: List the caller's Function definitions.
operations.notes: `tag` (query, optional) narrows the list to callables carrying that tag: a row is kept when one of its tags equals the value or starts with the value plus `.` (segment-bounded: `action.order` matches `action.order` and `action.order.confirm` but not `action.orders`). Sent as `?tag=<value>` ONLY when set and non-empty (an omitted or empty tag sends no query parameter, which is the unfiltered list); a single value, no multi-tag OR. Each row carries `tags: string[]` (`[]` when none); create/update definitions accept a top-level `tags?: string[]` (strings only, trimmed, empties dropped, de-duplicated; an update replaces the stored tags only when `tags` is supplied). The discovery operation for this domain, in for the same reason `workflows.list` and `connections.list` are (D4): it is how a caller finds the `key` to pass to `functions.run`. Unpaginated today, same as `workflows.list`. **NO `project` PARAM** — unlike workflows and documents this route reads no `?project=` at all (`admin/functions.ts` calls `repo.list(scope)` with none), and sending one would be inventing a parameter. Each row already carries `valid`, computed server-side by the same predicate the invoke path guards with, so runnability needs no second call. `displayName` falls back to `key` server-side and is never a substitute for it: `key` is what `functions.run` takes.

operations.name: functions.get
operations.summary: Fetch one Function's stored definition.
operations.notes: Takes an `fn_…` id OR a `key`, the same either-or `functions.run` takes and for the same reason: an id carries an underscore and a key's grammar forbids one, so the two cannot collide. Returns `{function, valid, updatedAt}` and wrappers MUST keep `valid` and `updatedAt` top-level siblings rather than splicing them into the definition — it is computed per request, it is not part of the stored document (`rfcs/function.md`), and folding it in would put it inside the object a caller sends straight back to `functions.update`. `updatedAt` is the concurrency token to pass to `functions.update` as `ifUnmodifiedSince`. (`console.functions.get` does splice both, for studio's sake; that is the console surface, not this one.) The definition stays OPAQUE: its `impl` is a union the server extends — an app Action, another Function, or a Workflow since D-8 — and the whole point of a Function is that `impl` is the part you swap. Missing id is `404 unknown_function`.

operations.name: functions.create
operations.summary: Create a Function definition.
operations.notes: The create half of the server's single upsert route (`POST /functions`). THE SERVER MINTS AN ID ONLY WHEN THE CALLER SENDS NONE — a caller-supplied `id` is accepted only if it matches `^fn_[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}$`, else `400 invalid_function` — so wrappers still mint `fn_<uuid>` client-side when the definition carries none, exactly as `workflows.create` does. `key` is NOT minted: it is the name the Function is CALLED by, so it is the caller's to choose. The server validates `key` on FIRST SAVE ONLY (3–39 chars, starts lowercase, lowercase letters/digits/single hyphens, no `_`), deliberately leaving legacy keys alone on update; that grammar is what keeps `/functions/{idOrKey}/invoke` unambiguous. `impl` is OPTIONAL — a Function with none is a valid draft that stores fine and answers `valid: false`, and wrappers must not require it. Returns `{id, key}` under a `function` envelope plus the first `updatedAt` as a TOP-LEVEL sibling of it (wrappers surface it as `{id, key, updatedAt}`); create takes no precondition — there is nothing yet to be stale against. `409 function_conflict` is an ownership clash on the id; `409 function_key_conflict` is the key already being taken — two distinct codes, and a wrapper must surface both rather than flattening them.

operations.name: functions.update
operations.summary: Overwrite a Function definition.
operations.notes: The update half of the same upsert route as `functions.create`. **A FULL REPLACEMENT, NOT A PATCH** — read with `functions.get`, change what you mean to change, send the whole thing back. `id` comes from the FIRST ARGUMENT and is pinned into the body, overriding any `id` the definition carries. `ifUnmodifiedSince` is the optimistic-concurrency precondition, sent as the `x-w6w-if-unmodified-since` HEADER (not a query param) and ONLY when a value was given — never as an empty or "null" string, which the server answers `400 invalid_precondition`. Pass the exact `updatedAt` from `functions.get` or a prior save; a stale one is `409 function_stale`, which IS recoverable by reloading and re-saving, unlike `409 function_conflict`, which is not. Omitted, the write is last-write-wins. The save answers the new `updatedAt` as a TOP-LEVEL sibling of the `function` envelope, so a caller can chain saves without a re-read. Do not send `valid` or `updatedAt` back: neither is part of the stored document, which is exactly why `functions.get` leaves them outside the definition.

operations.name: functions.delete
operations.summary: Delete a Function.
operations.notes: Takes an `fn_…` id or a `key`. The server returns `{ok: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code), same pin as `documents.delete`. NOT idempotent: deleting an id that is not there is `404 unknown_function`, and wrappers must not pretend otherwise. **ARCHIVE FIRST**, exactly like a workflow: a Function that is not `archived` yet is `409 function_not_archived` (see `functions.archive`), and a wrapper must NOT catch that and archive on the caller's behalf. **Nothing checks for callers first**: a Function may be referenced by an Endpoint, by a Workflow step, or by another Function's `impl` (D-8), and the server does not walk those references — they break at call time.

operations.name: functions.archive
operations.summary: Archive a Function — the required step before deleting it.
operations.notes: One-way: there is no unarchive route on this domain. Idempotent — archiving an already-archived Function re-returns it unchanged rather than erroring. Returns the definition under a `function` envelope and the wrapper UNWRAPS it. This is a PRECONDITION of `functions.delete`, not a convenience: deleting a Function that is not archived is `409 function_not_archived`. Missing id is `404 unknown_function`.

operations.name: functions.listVersions
operations.summary: List a function's published versions.
operations.notes: Returns the WHOLE body unchanged: `enabled`, `currentPublishedVersion` (`null` before the first publish) and `versions[]` (`versionNumber`, `createdAt`, `createdBy` — `null` when unknown — and `isCurrentPublished`). Metadata only: no `definition`; fetch one with `functions.getVersion`. Missing id is `404 unknown_function`.

operations.name: functions.getVersion
operations.summary: Read one published version of a function, with its definition.
operations.notes: The server answers `{version: {versionNumber, createdAt, createdBy, isCurrentPublished, definition}}` and the wrapper UNWRAPS the `version` key. `definition` is opaque and redacted server-side (a sealed secret envelope is never returned). `n` is the 1-based version number. Errors: `404 unknown_version`, `404 unknown_function`, `400 invalid_version` when `n` is not a positive integer.

operations.name: functions.publish
operations.summary: Publish the function's stored definition as a new immutable version.
operations.notes: Returns the WHOLE body: `{version: {kind, callableId, versionNumber, createdAt, createdBy}, currentPublishedVersion}`. Publish snapshots the STORED row, not whatever an editor holds in memory, so a caller must flush any pending save first. No precondition is taken: nothing checks that the row changed since the last publish. Errors: `404 unknown_function`.

operations.name: functions.revert
operations.summary: Rewrite the live function from a published version.
operations.notes: The server answers `{reverted: {kind, callableId, versionNumber}}` and the wrapper UNWRAPS the `reverted` key. Revert itself is unguarded, but it rewrites the stored row, so its `updatedAt` moves: a token read before a revert is stale after it (`409 function_stale` on the next guarded `functions.update`). It does not publish: the live row becomes a draft that matches version `n` until `functions.publish` is called. Errors: `404 unknown_version`, `404 unknown_function`, `400 invalid_version`.

operations.name: functions.enable
operations.summary: Enable the function's invocability.
operations.notes: The server returns `{enabled: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code). Idempotent. A disabled function is refused by every run, version runs and `allowUnpublished` draft runs included (`function_disabled`). Missing id is `404 unknown_function`.

operations.name: functions.disable
operations.summary: Disable the function's invocability.
operations.notes: The server returns `{enabled: false}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code). Idempotent. A disabled function is refused by every run, version runs and `allowUnpublished` draft runs included (`function_disabled`). Missing id is `404 unknown_function`.

operations.name: functions.runVersion
operations.summary: Run one published version of a Function and return its output.
operations.notes: Same body as `functions.run`, against ONE published version instead of the live row. The wire verb is `invoke` (not `run`): `POST /functions/{id}/versions/{n}/invoke`. Returns the Function's OUTPUT unwrapped from the `output` envelope, exactly as `functions.run` does (guard on PRESENCE of the key, a `null` output is a successful run); wrappers expose the body field as `payload` and send it as `inputs`. Errors: `404 unknown_version`, `404 unknown_function`, `422 function_incomplete`, `422 function_disabled`, `422 function_not_published`, `400 invalid_version`.

operations.name: endpoints.list
operations.summary: List the caller's Endpoint definitions.
operations.notes: The discovery operation for the Endpoint domain, mirroring `functions.list`: it is how a caller finds the `key` to pass to `endpoints.run`, and the way tag mode reaches Endpoints. Unpaginated; **NO `project` PARAM**, same as `functions.list`. Returns the `endpoints` array unwrapped. Each row carries `tags: string[]` (`[]` when none). `tag` (query, optional) narrows the list to callables carrying that tag: a row is kept when one of its tags equals the value or starts with the value plus `.` (segment-bounded: `action.order` matches `action.order` and `action.order.confirm` but not `action.orders`). Sent as `?tag=<value>` ONLY when set and non-empty (an omitted or empty tag sends no query parameter, which is the unfiltered list); a single value, no multi-tag OR. This is the stable list op; the CLI's `w6w ls endpoints` keeps listing through the unstable `console.endpoints` namespace.

operations.name: endpoints.run
operations.summary: Run one Endpoint by its key (or id); the envelope's kind says which arm answered.
operations.notes: Name-first, exactly like `functions.run`; wrappers expose the body field as `payload` though the wire spells it `input` (singular here, plural for a Function). UNLIKE `functions.run` this returns the kind-discriminated `RunEnvelope`, and the asymmetry is deliberate: an Endpoint dispatches to an app action, a Function or a Workflow, so only the response says which answered — the discriminant is information, not ceremony. The workflow arm returns 202, which is a NORMAL outcome and not an error. Wrappers must tolerate an unknown future `kind` rather than crashing, the same rule the unified `run` carries. The `{idOrKey}` path segment takes EITHER the resource's host-issued id or the key the user gave it, with no prefix, flag or tag to say which — the two shapes cannot collide, because an id carries a kind prefix and therefore an underscore while a key is a kebab-slug that forbids one. Resolution is id-first (a pure prefix test, no query), so this path cannot be used to probe whether a key exists by supplying something id-shaped. Two unknown KEYS answer identically and neither is echoed back — a key is short, human-chosen and guessable, so echoing it would make this an enumeration oracle; an unknown id may still be echoed, since nobody guesses a uuid. The key is unique per ACCOUNT, so within the scope a credential carries it names exactly one resource. INVOCATION FRAME (server, 2026-08-20): every arm of this envelope now also carries `invocationId` (an `inv_…` id for THIS attempt), `status`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt` and `durationMs`, and the two synchronous arms carry `output` — on the action arm alongside the existing `value`, which is now a DEPRECATED MIRROR of it and keeps the same meaning. Every one of those fields is ADDITIVE: no field was renamed, removed or re-typed, so an installed wrapper written against the three-arm shape keeps working unchanged. `status` is the PLATFORM's verdict on the attempt (`succeeded` | `failed` | `queued`) and must not be confused with a status the target itself reported inside `output`. `invocationId` and `runId` are DIFFERENT ids and neither replaces the other: `invocationId` names the attempt and resolves through `GET /invocations/{id}`; `runId` stays the queued workflow run on the workflow arm alone. A FAILED call's 4xx body carries the same frame fields beside its `error`, so the attempt is still lookup-able. New callers should read `output` on every arm.

operations.name: team.members.list
operations.summary: List the caller's account team: every active member and their role.
operations.notes: Server wraps the body as `{ members: TeamMember[] }`; the wrapper unwraps and returns the array. Not project-scoped — team membership is an account-wide concept, and this route takes no `?project=`. Roster viewing is member-readable: any active member of the caller's account may list it, regardless of role — only the write operations below are gated by `canManageMembers`.

operations.name: team.invites.create
operations.summary: Invite someone to the caller's account, or mint an open, shareable invite link.
operations.notes: `email` is optional: omitted, the server mints an OPEN invite — a shareable link with no target address, redeemable by whoever holds it. `role` defaults server-side to `"member"` when omitted, and `"owner"` is refused (`400 invalid_role`) — there is no self-service path to a second owner. Requires `canManageMembers` (`403 forbidden` otherwise). The response's `token` and `redemptionLink` are returned exactly once, at creation — they are never re-fetchable from `team.invites.list`, so a caller that drops this response has to revoke and re-invite. Server wraps the body as `{ invite: TeamInviteWithLink }`.

operations.name: team.invites.list
operations.summary: List the caller's account's open (pending, unrevoked, unexpired) invites.
operations.notes: Server wraps the body as `{ invites: TeamInvite[] }`; the wrapper unwraps and returns the array, already filtered server-side to OPEN invites only (not used, not revoked, not expired) — this is one HTTP call, never a client-side list-then-filter over every invite the account has ever issued. Any active member of the account may list open invites, regardless of role — member-readable, like the roster.

operations.name: team.invites.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke a pending invite before it is redeemed.
operations.notes: The server returns `{ok: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code), same pin as `documents.delete`. Requires `canManageMembers` (`403 forbidden` otherwise). `404 invite_not_found` for an unknown id; `409 invite_not_open` for one already used or already revoked — revoking is NOT idempotent and wrappers must not pretend otherwise.

operations.name: team.members.updateRole
operations.summary: Change a team member's role.
operations.notes: Requires `canManageMembers` (`403 forbidden` otherwise). `role` of `"owner"` is refused (`403 cannot_change_owner_role`) and so is retargeting the account's current owner — there is no self-service ownership transfer. `400 invalid_role` for anything outside the account role set; `404 member_not_found` for an unknown `userId`. Server wraps the body as `{ member: TeamMember }`.

operations.name: team.members.remove
operations.summary: Remove a member from the caller's account.
operations.notes: The server returns `{ok: true}` and the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING (`void` / `None` / exit code), same pin as `documents.delete`. This TOMBSTONES the membership rather than deleting the row (D-R3) — a removed member's `userId` may still appear in historical records — but that is a server-side implementation detail the wrapper contract does not surface. Requires `canManageMembers` (`403 forbidden` otherwise). The account's owner cannot be removed (`403 cannot_remove_owner`), and removing the account's last active member is refused (`409 last_member`) rather than leaving an ownerless, memberless account. `404 member_not_found` for an unknown `userId`.

operations.name: apps.byIds
operations.summary: Resolve a set of app ids to their catalog summaries.

params.name: ids
params.$comment: The wire value is a comma-separated list (`ids=a,b`). The wrapper takes an array.

operations.notes: Bounded lookup, not catalog browsing: the server caps `ids` at 100 per request and answers `400 too_many_ids` beyond that, so the wrapper CHUNKS to 100 client-side (one `GET /apps?ids=a,b,...` per chunk, issued concurrently, results concatenated in chunk order) and the cap never reaches a caller. Duplicate ids are collapsed first. An empty set returns `[]` with NO request at all (never an unfiltered page). The server unwraps the page envelope `{apps, nextCursor}`; the wrapper returns the `apps` of every chunk. Unknown ids are simply absent. Where the app belongs to a connection, the inline `app` object on `connections.list` / `connections.get` is the PRIMARY icon and label source and needs no extra request; use `apps.byIds` for ids that do not come from a connection. Catalog browse / search / paging is out of scope.

operations.name: dashboard.stats
operations.summary: Account-scoped dashboard rollup over the run ledger.
operations.notes: Account-scoped: the account comes from the credential, there is NO `project` parameter and the client's default project is never sent. The response has no envelope key; the rollup (`range`, `headline`, `series`, `recent`) IS the body. `from` / `to` are ISO-8601 instants and `bucket` is `day` or `week`; each is sent only when given and the server applies its own defaults otherwise. `knownValues` on `bucket` is documentation, not a constraint.

operations.name: projects.list
operations.summary: List the account's active projects.
operations.notes: Server wraps the body as `{ projects: Project[] }`; the wrapper unwraps and returns the array. READ-ONLY: project create, rename, archive and delete are not in this contract. Archived projects are not listed. Each row carries `isDefault`. SIDE EFFECT: the GET ensures the account's default project exists and creates it when there is none, so a first call on a fresh account returns one `isDefault: true` row, not `[]`.

operations.name: reliability.list
operations.summary: Reliability board for a project and an explicit set of apps.

params.name: apps
params.$comment: Comma-separated app ids on the wire; the wrapper takes an array of at most 10.

params.name: days
params.$comment: A positive integer number of days; sent as a query string.

params.name: limit
params.$comment: A positive integer cap; sent as a query string.

operations.notes: The response has no envelope key: the board IS the body. The server accepts AT MOST 10 app ids (`apps` is required and must hold 1 to 10 ids); anything else is `400 invalid_app_filter`, and a missing `project` is `400 missing_project`. The wrapper sends exactly the ids it is given and surfaces the server's 400 as `ApiError` unchanged; it has NO batching helper, so splitting a larger set (via `reliability.members`) across calls, and scheduling or polling them, is the host's job. Services are ordered most-urgent first, then by last call; `limit` caps after that ordering. `days` and `limit` are sent only when given.

operations.name: reliability.members
operations.summary: List the app ids a project's calls touch.

params.name: days
params.$comment: A positive integer number of days; sent as a query string.

operations.notes: Identifier-only membership discovery: no status probes are made. The response has no envelope key; `appIds` is the list to feed, at most 10 at a time, to `reliability.list`. `project` is required (`400 missing_project` otherwise). `days` is sent only when given.

operations.name: run
operations.summary: Run anything addressable by URN — a connection action, a function, an endpoint or a workflow.
operations.notes: D3 — `RunEnvelope` is kind-discriminated with exactly three arms: `{kind:"action", value}` | `{kind:"function", output}` | `{kind:"workflow", runId, status}`. The action and function arms return 200; the workflow arm returns 202, and 202 is a NORMAL outcome, not an error — the run is queued, and `runId` is how the caller follows it. Wrappers must switch on `kind` and must tolerate an unknown future `kind` rather than crashing. `action` is optional because a workflow, function or endpoint URN has no action; it is required in practice for a `conn_…` URN. `urn` resolves over the `conn_`, `wf_`, `fn_` and `ep_` arms (D16), and, additionally, an account-scoped alias name (kebab-slug, `_`-free, which is why no flag is needed to disambiguate the two); `doc_` and `var_` are NOT URN arms in v0.1.0 and are addressed by the `documents.*` / `vars.*` operations above. This is deliberately narrower than `workflows.run`: `?wait=`, `variables` and `trigger` have no slot in the three-field `{urn, action, payload}` shape (D4). Server-implemented 2026-07-28: a third sibling BLL service dispatching to the same runners the dedicated invoke routes use — no new execution path, no change to core Callable. INVOCATION FRAME (server, 2026-08-20): every arm of this envelope now also carries `invocationId` (an `inv_…` id for THIS attempt), `status`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt` and `durationMs`, and the two synchronous arms carry `output` — on the action arm alongside the existing `value`, which is now a DEPRECATED MIRROR of it and keeps the same meaning. Every one of those fields is ADDITIVE: no field was renamed, removed or re-typed, so an installed wrapper written against the three-arm shape keeps working unchanged. `status` is the PLATFORM's verdict on the attempt (`succeeded` | `failed` | `queued`) and must not be confused with a status the target itself reported inside `output`. `invocationId` and `runId` are DIFFERENT ids and neither replaces the other: `invocationId` names the attempt and resolves through `GET /invocations/{id}`; `runId` stays the queued workflow run on the workflow arm alone. A FAILED call's 4xx body carries the same frame fields beside its `error`, so the attempt is still lookup-able. New callers should read `output` on every arm.

operations.name: models.list
operations.summary: List the model catalog (keyset-paged).
operations.notes: Server answers `{ models: Model[], nextCursor }`; the wrapper returns that page object as-is (a keyset page, so the cursor is not discarded). `status` is `active|deprecated|blocked`. Errors: `400 invalid_limit`, `400 invalid_cursor`. Catalog PATCH, rates, discover and `/models/providers` are node `console` group only.

operations.name: models.get
operations.summary: Fetch one catalog model by id.
operations.notes: Addressed by the server-issued catalog id (`mdl_…`), not by a provider-native model id such as `gpt-4o`. Server wraps the body as `{ model: Model }`; the wrapper unwraps. `Model` carries `currentRate` (`ModelRate | null`). Unknown id is the uniform `404`.

operations.name: modelRoutes.list
operations.summary: List the caller's model routes in a project.
operations.notes: Models are catalog rows; `?project=` resolves like `documents.*` (`400 unknown_project`). Server wraps the body as `{ routes: ModelRoute[] }`; the wrapper unwraps. Route create/update/delete are node `console` group only. At 0.18.0 each route may carry `credentialMode: "account" | "invoking_user"`, `credentialSelection` (`{mode:"account",connectionId}` | `{mode:"invoking_user"}`) and `connectionId: string | null` (null for an `invoking_user` route); each fallback carries the same.

operations.name: modelRoutes.get
operations.summary: Fetch one model route by name.
operations.notes: Models are catalog rows; `?project=` resolves like `documents.*` (`400 unknown_project`). Addressed by route `name`. Server wraps the body as `{ route: ModelRoute }`; the wrapper unwraps. Missing name is `404 model_route_not_found`. At 0.18.0 the route may carry `credentialMode: "account" | "invoking_user"`, `credentialSelection` (`{mode:"account",connectionId}` | `{mode:"invoking_user"}`) and `connectionId: string | null` (null for an `invoking_user` route); each fallback carries the same.

operations.name: modelRoutes.complete
operations.summary: Run a completion through a model route.
operations.notes: POSTs the `BridgeInput` body as-is. Returns the FLAT envelope `{ contractVersion (1), route (string|null), provider, key, model, dialect, output?, usage, usageSummary, raw?, meta (meta.usageRecorded: boolean), invocationId, status, startedAt, finishedAt, durationMs }` exactly as the server sends it: NO unwrap to `output` (`key` is the answering connection id, `invocationId`/`status` are the standard invocation frame). `dialect` is `bridge|openai|anthropic|ollama` (`bridge` is the provider-neutral baseline output) and `usageSummary` is `{ inclusiveInputTokens, freshInputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, outputTokens, reasoningTokens, totalTokens: number|null; source: reported|partial|estimated|unknown|legacy }` identical across providers; and `response` is `both|output|raw` (typed unions in node, documented in python); `response=output` omits `raw`, `response=raw` omits `output`. Each is sent only when given. Errors: `400 model_request_unsupported` (carries `capability`), `429 model_budget_exceeded`, `424 model_provider_failed`, `409 model_route_broken`, `403 model_egress_denied`, `404 model_route_not_found`. A provider failure that the server reports as an invocation frame is the lane's ordinary API error. At 0.18.0 the error codes `personal_key_required`, `personal_key_unavailable`, `ai_credential_policy_denied` and `user_context_required` were added.

operations.name: modelUsage.query
operations.summary: Query recorded model usage, optionally grouped.

naming.python: client.model_usage.query(project=None, group_by=None, from_=None, to=None, route=None, model=None, limit=None, cursor=None)

operations.notes: Models are catalog rows; `?project=` resolves like `documents.*` (`400 unknown_project`). Returns the body as-is: `{ totals: { requests, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens, cacheWriteTokens, totalTokens, cost: [{ currency, amountMinor }], unpriced }, totalsTruncated, groups?: [{ key, requests, totalTokens, cost }], items: ModelUsage[], nextCursor }`. `totalsTruncated` is `true` when the server stopped folding the ledger at its aggregate row cap, so `totals`/`groups` cover only part of the window. `groupBy` is `route|model|day` and adds `groups`. The query keys are sent as `groupBy`/`from`/`to`/`route`/`model`/`limit`/`cursor` (python's `group_by`/`from_` are renamed on the wire). Budgets CRUD and `/model-budgets/:id/usage` are node `console` group only.

operations.name: assets.uploads.create
operations.summary: Reserve a resumable asset upload (declare the entries; no bytes yet).

naming.python: client.assets.uploads.create(purpose, idempotency_key, entries, name=None, visibility=None, asset_id=None, target=None)

operations.notes: `/asset-uploads` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found` — never a distinct 403. Body `{purpose, idempotencyKey, entries:[{path, sizeBytes, sha256, mediaType?}], name?, visibility?, assetId?, target?}`: `purpose` is `asset|skill|context`, `visibility` is `private|project|account` (default `private`, ignored when `assetId` names an existing asset), `assetId` publishes a new version of that asset instead of creating one, `target` is purpose-specific destination data persisted verbatim (e.g. `{skillId}` / `{collectionId}`). `entries[].sha256` is lowercase hex and `sizeBytes` a non-negative safe integer; the order of `entries` fixes each entry's `index`. Returns `{upload, entries}` exactly as sent (`AssetUploadStatus`, no unwrap) — `201` when created, `200` when `idempotencyKey` replays the identical request (both are success; the wrapper does not surface which). `archive: true` (ZIP as the single entry) is refused `422 archive_upload_unavailable` until the host wires the zip reader; wrappers do not send it. Errors: `400 invalid_body`, `413 too_many_files`, `413 quota_exceeded`, `422 validation_failed`, `409 conflict`, `503 managed_storage_unavailable`.

operations.name: assets.uploads.putEntry
operations.summary: Send one declared entry's raw bytes.
operations.notes: `/asset-uploads` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found` — never a distinct 403. BYTES IN: the request body is the entry's raw bytes with `content-type: application/octet-stream` — never JSON-encoded, quoted or base64'd (`bodyEncoding: "octet-stream"`, docs/endpoints.md Conventions). The server reads at most `min(declared size, effective maxFileBytes)` and verifies the sha256 against the declaration; a mismatch is `422 validation_failed` (an over-cap entry `413`), an oversize body `413 payload_too_large`, an upload no longer `open` `409 conflict`, an unknown `index` `422 validation_failed`. Re-sending an entry already received is allowed (the reserve view's `state` says which are `received`). The server answers `{entry}`; the wrapper unwraps it to the `AssetUploadEntry`.

operations.name: assets.uploads.finalize
operations.summary: Publish a fully received upload as an asset version.
operations.notes: `/asset-uploads` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found` — never a distinct 403. Idempotent: a second call on an already-published upload returns the same version and charges nothing (`created: false`). Returns the flat `{uploadId, assetId, versionId, version, readiness, derived, created}` as sent — no unwrap. `readiness` is `ready` or `pending` (a version whose bytes are not yet durable at its destination publishes `pending`; poll `assets.versions`). `derived` is what the purpose handler extracted (a skill/context result), or `null`. Errors: `409 conflict` (upload not `open`, expired, or entries missing), `422 validation_failed` (the package failed validation; over-cap packages `413 too_large`), `413 quota_exceeded`.

operations.name: assets.uploads.get
operations.summary: Read an upload's status and per-entry state (the resume point).
operations.notes: `/asset-uploads` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found` — never a distinct 403. Returns `{upload, entries}` as sent. Each entry carries `state` (`pending|received`) and `receivedAt`; a client resuming an interrupted upload (`w6w assets upload --retry`) skips every entry already `received`.

operations.name: assets.uploads.abort
operations.summary: Abort an open upload and release its reservation.
operations.notes: `/asset-uploads` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found` — never a distinct 403. Despite being a `DELETE` this answers `200 {upload, entries}` (the aborted upload's final view), not `{ok:true}`, and the wrapper returns it as-is. Aborting an upload that is already published or aborted is `409 conflict`.

operations.name: assets.get
operations.summary: Fetch one asset.
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. The server wraps the body as `{asset}`; the wrapper unwraps. Never carries a storage path, object key or binding coordinate.

operations.name: assets.versions
operations.summary: List an asset's versions.
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. The server wraps the body as `{versions}`; the wrapper unwraps. A `failed` version is never listed. `readiness` is `pending|ready`, `syncState` the destination-sync state.

operations.name: assets.files
operations.summary: List the files of one asset version.
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Returns `{version, files}` as sent (`AssetVersionFiles`, no unwrap). A version that does not belong to the asset is the uniform `404`. Files carry `id, path, mediaType, sizeBytes, sha256, createdAt` and never an object key.

operations.name: assets.content
operations.summary: Download one file's raw bytes.
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. BYTES OUT (`responseEncoding: "octet-stream"`): returns the file's body byte-for-byte as `Uint8Array` (node/cli) / `bytes` (python) — never decoded as text or JSON, so a non-UTF-8 sequence such as `\xff\xfe\x00` survives. The server sends the file's own media type with `content-disposition: attachment` and `nosniff`; the wrapper ignores them. A non-2xx still carries the JSON error envelope and raises the typed error with its `code`. The CLI writes to `--out` or, absent that, stdout.

operations.name: assets.archiveDownload
operations.summary: Download one version as a store-only ZIP.
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. BYTES OUT (`responseEncoding: "octet-stream"`): a store-only ZIP of the version's files, returned unmodified as `Uint8Array` / `bytes`. Pinned by plan §P6 but NOT yet served by the host (`serverImplemented: false`): against a host without the route the call raises the ordinary `404`. Errors in byte mode parse the JSON envelope like any other route.

operations.name: assets.archive
operations.summary: Archive an asset (retire it from listings; bytes are kept).
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Returns the archived asset (`archivedAt` set), unwrapped from the server's `{asset}`. Archiving never deletes bytes; that is `assets.purge`. A caller who may not manage the asset gets the uniform `404 not_found`.

operations.name: assets.purge
operations.summary: Permanently delete an asset, its versions and their bytes (account admin only).
operations.notes: `/assets` routes are principal-scoped: a missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Irreversible. Returns `{assetId, versionsDeleted, objectsDeleted}` as sent — no unwrap. Only an account admin may purge — anyone else gets the uniform `404 not_found`, not a 403. An asset still referenced by a skill version or context entry is refused `409 purge_refused` (the envelope also carries `skillVersionIds` and `contextEntryIds`).

operations.name: skills.list
operations.summary: List skills visible to the caller.
operations.notes: Principal-scoped. The server wraps the body as `{skills}`; the wrapper unwraps. Archived skills are omitted unless `includeArchived` is true. Never carries a storage path or object key. Skills are CREATED by uploading with `assets.uploads.create` and `purpose: "skill"` — there is no `skills.create`.

operations.name: skills.get
operations.summary: Fetch one skill.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. The server wraps the body as `{skill}`; the wrapper unwraps. `activeVersionId` is the version new pins should target; existing agent pins are unaffected by a new version.

operations.name: skills.versions
operations.summary: List a skill's versions.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. The server wraps the body as `{versions}`; the wrapper unwraps. A `SkillVersion.id` is what an agent's `skills[].skillVersionId` pins.

operations.name: skills.archive
operations.summary: Archive a skill (retire it from listings).
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Returns the archived skill (`archivedAt` set), unwrapped from `{skill}`. A caller who may not manage the skill gets the uniform `404`. Archiving never deletes bytes.

operations.name: context.list
operations.summary: List context collections visible to the caller.
operations.notes: Principal-scoped. The server wraps the body as `{collections}`; the wrapper unwraps. Archived collections are omitted unless `includeArchived` is true.

operations.name: context.create
operations.summary: Create a context collection.
operations.notes: `visibility` is `private|project|account`; anything else is `400 invalid_body`. The server wraps the body as `{collection}`; the wrapper unwraps. A collection starts empty — add entries with `context.entries.create` or upload files with `assets.uploads.create` and `purpose: "context"`.

operations.name: context.get
operations.summary: Fetch one context collection.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Unwrapped from `{collection}`.

operations.name: context.update
operations.summary: Patch a context collection's name, description or tags.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Every body field is optional; an omitted field is left alone. `visibility` is NOT patchable here. Unlike the entry and agent writes, a collection patch carries NO precondition and NO `revision` (last-write-wins). Unwrapped from `{collection}`.

operations.name: context.archive
operations.summary: Archive a context collection.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Returns the archived collection (`archivedAt` set), unwrapped from `{collection}`.

operations.name: context.entries.list
operations.summary: List the entries of a context collection.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. `id` is the COLLECTION id. The server wraps the body as `{entries}`; the wrapper unwraps. A listed entry carries NO `revision` and NO `previewable` — those ride only on the `ContextEntryView` that `context.entries.create` / `context.entries.update` answer. `assetVersionId` is the pin id an agent's `context[].assetVersionId` attaches.

operations.name: context.entries.create
operations.summary: Add a text entry to a context collection.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. `id` is the COLLECTION id. Both `name` and `text` must be strings (`400 invalid_body`); the text is size-capped by the server. Answers the new entry as a `ContextEntryView` (with `revision`, the token for the first `context.entries.update`), unwrapped from `{entry}`. Binary entries are uploads (`assets.uploads.create`, `purpose: "context"`), not this op.

operations.name: context.entries.update
operations.summary: Replace a text entry's content.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. A FULL REPLACEMENT of the text, not a patch. `id` is the COLLECTION id; an entry that does not belong to it is the uniform `404`. Body `revision` (a positive integer — the entry's last-seen revision) is REQUIRED and is passed through unchanged; a non-integer or `< 1` is `400 invalid_body`. `ifUnmodifiedSince` is the optimistic-concurrency precondition, sent as the `x-w6w-if-unmodified-since` HEADER (not a query param) and ONLY when a value was given — never as an empty or "null" string, which the server answers `400 invalid_precondition`. Pass the exact `updatedAt` last read. THE SERVER REQUIRES IT on this route: omitted, the answer is `428 precondition_required` (a typed precondition error, never a silent last-write-wins), so a wrapper must not default it. A stale `revision` or a stale `updatedAt` is `409 conflict` (recoverable: re-read and re-send); wrappers surface it as a typed conflict error, the 428 as a typed precondition error. Answers the new `ContextEntryView` (with the bumped `revision`), unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: contextEntries.list
operations.summary: List context entries visible to the caller, across collections.
operations.notes: Top-level, collection-independent: an entry need not belong to any collection. `collectionId` filters to one collection's members. The server wraps the body as `{entries}`; the wrapper unwraps. A top-level entry carries `collectionIds` (sorted ascending) and never `collectionId`.

operations.name: contextEntries.create
operations.summary: Create a text entry, optionally in collections.
operations.notes: Both `name` and `text` must be strings. `visibility` defaults to the creator's default; `collectionIds` makes the entry a member of each. Answers the new `ContextEntryView` (with `revision`), unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: contextEntries.get
operations.summary: Fetch one context entry.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, invisible or other-project entry (or collection) is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: contextEntries.update
operations.summary: Replace a text entry's content.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, invisible or other-project entry (or collection) is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Same semantics as `context.entries.update`: a FULL REPLACEMENT; body `revision` required; `ifUnmodifiedSince` sent as the `x-w6w-if-unmodified-since` header only when given. The server REQUIRES it: omitted is `428 precondition_required`; a stale `revision` or `updatedAt` is `409 conflict`. Unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: contextEntries.archive
operations.summary: Archive a context entry.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, invisible or other-project entry (or collection) is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Returns the archived entry (`archivedAt` set), unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: contextEntries.addToCollection
operations.summary: Add an entry to a collection.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, invisible or other-project entry (or collection) is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Idempotent. Answers the entry with its updated `collectionIds`, unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: contextEntries.removeFromCollection
operations.summary: Remove an entry from a collection.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, invisible or other-project entry (or collection) is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Idempotent. Answers the entry with its updated `collectionIds`, unwrapped from `{entry}`.

operations.name: agents.list
operations.summary: List agent drafts visible to the caller.
operations.notes: Principal-scoped. The server wraps the body as `{agents}`; the wrapper unwraps. **Every Agent answers `runnable: false`** — an Agent here is a saved DRAFT; no Agent runtime, RAG or chat history exists (A22), and no op in this group runs one.

operations.name: agents.create
operations.summary: Create an agent draft.

naming.python: client.agents.create(name=None, instructions=None, model_route_id=None, skills=None, context=None, visibility=None, project=None, model_options=None, tools=None)

operations.notes: Saving an INCOMPLETE draft is allowed: every field is optional, and `validation` on the answer lists what is missing or disallowed. `skills` is `[{skillId, skillVersionId}]` and `context` is `[{collectionId, entryId?, assetVersionId}]` — pins to immutable VERSIONS, so a later skill upload never changes an existing pin. `instructions` is capped at 64 KiB, at most 100 pins. `tools` is `[{kind:"action", uses:{app, action, connection?}} | {kind:"function", function} | {kind:"workflow", workflow}]`, each with an optional `name` (1–64 chars, stored trimmed — what the model calls the tool; unique per agent, case-insensitive) an optional `description` (≤1024 chars, the author override of what the model is told), an optional `ai` (the field keys the model fills — the only ones in the tool schema and passed on) and an optional `with` (fixed field values, literals or expressions resolved by the host; a key is in `ai` or `with`, not both; ≤64 KiB); at most 50, no duplicate (kind, target); the response `Agent.tools` is always present (`[]` when none). A malformed or duplicate tool is `422 validation_failed`. A malformed body is `422 validation_failed` (the envelope carries `issues`). The server wraps the body as `{agent}`; the wrapper unwraps. **`runnable` is always `false`** (A22).

operations.name: agents.get
operations.summary: Fetch one agent draft.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Unwrapped from `{agent}`. Carries `revision` and `updatedAt` — the two tokens `agents.update` needs — and `runnable: false` (A22).

operations.name: agents.update
operations.summary: Patch an agent draft.

naming.python: client.agents.update(id, revision, name=None, instructions=None, model_route_id=None, skills=None, context=None, visibility=None, project=None, if_unmodified_since=None, model_options=None, tools=None)

operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. A partial update: an omitted field is left alone. Body `revision` (a positive integer — the draft's last-seen `revision`) is REQUIRED and is passed through unchanged; `< 1` or non-integer is `400 invalid_body`. `ifUnmodifiedSince` is the optimistic-concurrency precondition, sent as the `x-w6w-if-unmodified-since` HEADER (not a query param) and ONLY when a value was given — never as an empty or "null" string, which the server answers `400 invalid_precondition`. Pass the exact `updatedAt` last read. THE SERVER REQUIRES IT on this route: omitted, the answer is `428 precondition_required` (a typed precondition error, never a silent last-write-wins), so a wrapper must not default it. A stale `revision` or `updatedAt` is `409 conflict` carrying `currentRevision` in the error envelope (`{error:{code,message,currentRevision}}`) — recoverable by re-reading and re-sending; wrappers surface it as a typed conflict error carrying that revision, the 428 as a typed precondition error. A disallowed pin is `422 validation_failed` (a uniform 422, `issues` in the envelope). Unwrapped from `{agent}`; `runnable` stays `false` (A22). `tools`, when present, REPLACES the whole list; absent leaves it unchanged (same `tools` shape and limits as `agents.create`).

operations.name: agents.archive
operations.summary: Archive an agent draft.
operations.notes: A missing, foreign, private-to-someone-else or other-project id is the one uniform `404 not_found`. Returns the archived draft (`archived: true`), unwrapped from `{agent}`. There is no agent delete or purge op.

operations.name: appManagement.list
operations.summary: List the apps the caller manages, with live management state per row.

params.name: scope
params.$comment: `all` (default), `account`, `tenant` or `personal`.

params.name: q
params.$comment: Search text.

params.name: sort
params.$comment: `name` (default), `-name`, `recent` or `-recent`.

params.name: compact
params.$comment: Compact rows.

params.name: snapshot
params.$comment: A previous page's snapshot token.

params.name: cursor
params.$comment: The previous page's `nextCursor`.

params.name: offset
params.$comment: Row offset.

params.name: limit
params.$comment: Page size.

naming.python: client.app_management.list(scope=None, q=None, sort=None, compact=None, snapshot=None, cursor=None, offset=None, limit=None)

operations.notes: Nothing is unwrapped: the body is returned exactly as sent. The envelope is `{apps, scope, snapshot, total, offset, limit, expiresAt, nextCursor?, targets, sourceOptions}`: `targets` is always three `TargetOption`s (account, tenant, personal) and `sourceOptions` is what the caller may name as a source. Each row is the catalog summary plus `management`, `source` and `lastSync`, computed live. `ManagementClass`, `UnavailableReason` and `TargetOption.reason` are open unions (a newer server may add values); `SyncOutcome` is closed. Each option is sent under its own name only when given, so `offset: 0` and `compact: false` are sent. Codes: `400 invalid_scope`, `400 invalid_query`, `400 invalid_cursor`, `400 invalid_limit`, `400 invalid_offset`, `403 forbidden` (`scope=tenant` from a non-admin), `404 unknown_snapshot`, `410 snapshot_expired`, `400 snapshot_query_mismatch`. `snapshot` and `cursor` are mutually exclusive.
